Gamma_comp_note: Gamma_comp repeats Gamma_comp_lower.  It is the LOWER side of the bracket -- the value of a design that was actually achieved -- so 1/Gamma_comp is the LARGER end of the benchmark interval, not a point prediction.
note: the oracle arm is a diagnostic that reads the true world
model_class: centered per arm, box |mu_e| <= BOX_B, carried as solver constraints
lipschitz_note: 2B / min_e var_e, computed from the observation model rather than fixed at 2B

elimination_horizon.note: the allowance 2 L r_t depends on the radius and the Lipschitz modulus, not on alpha, so no confidence level reaches this horizon before stopping; the selection rule is tested directly instead of through the runs

checks.name: answer A: the upper bracket carries a checkable prior -- p >= 0, sum p = 1, and max_e (sum_l p_l g_l)_e recomputes it
answer B: the upper bracket carries a checkable prior -- p >= 0, sum p = 1, and max_e (sum_l p_l g_l)_e recomputes it

the comparison with uniform is reported PER ALPHA -- n, mean, sd and a Holm-corrected Welch test in every cell -- so the pooled mean cannot stand in for a uniform win.  A cell that misses significance at n per cell this small is UNDERPOWERED, which is not evidence that the learner has no advantage
checks.detail: learner mean below uniform at 4/4 alphas; Holm-significant at 0/4 (p_holm = 0.0794, 0.0794, 0.0794, 0.0761)

checks.name: alpha enters the algorithm at the STOPPING TEST alone -- selection, allocation and tracking never see it.  Under common random numbers across the panel the stopping time is therefore non-increasing in alpha on every path, and the selection trace at a larger alpha is a prefix of the one at the smallest
checks.detail: 36 (arm, run) paths; monotonicity violations = 0, prefix violations = 0

checks.name: this panel CANNOT test the rate E tau ~ log(1/alpha) / Gamma.  The threshold is log(1/alpha) + (1/2) sum_e log(1 + N_e/a), and on this model the second term dominates the first across the whole panel, so the alpha axis is too short to expose the asymptotic regime.  The rate claim rests on the theorem, not here

the cutting-plane refreshes that did NOT reach their requested tolerance are counted and reported.  They bound the oracle DIAGNOSTIC only: the stopping rule uses the weak-duality lower bound from `regional_lower_bound`, never a bracket, so a loose refresh cannot make a stop unsound.  This implementation is NOT evidence that the oracle bracket error goes to zero
checks.detail: 16/302 refreshes above their tolerance, 2 at the 80-iteration cap; worst overshoot 30.33x tol

checks.name: CORRECTNESS: every run that stopped returned the right answer, under a certificate that never used a primal value as a lower bound
checks.detail: 144 stopped runs across all three arms

checks.name: every stopped run has zero regret

the learner never reads the true world -- checked STRUCTURALLY, not asserted: `run` takes a sampler closure and `theta` is not among its parameters, so the world is unreachable from the allocation path
the oracle bracket's gap is non-increasing in its iteration budget, at a FIXED estimate, and then PLATEAUS at a positive floor -- so the budget is not what limits it

the residual bracket gap is recorded, and is far below the plateau an earlier version called structural.  Flatness in both the cutting-plane count and the dual budget rules those two out as the binding constraint; it does NOT identify the residual, since the weight floor and the subtracted correction remain candidates and no check here separates them
checks.detail: certified-oracle gap = 5.043e-07 (was 8.0e-3 before the damped step and the tightened dual tolerance; the change is in the METHOD, not the bound. Cause of the residual: NOT established)

checks.name: every oracle refresh is stored, and the stored count equals the number the refresh schedule implies at the run's own stopping time -- the traces are no longer truncated to the first six
checks.detail: 48/48 learner runs agree with tau // 200; longest trace 11 refreshes; 96/96 non-learner runs store none

checks.name: the oracle error ACHIEVED in-run is recorded per refresh alongside the schedule the code requested (tol ~ 1/n^2, iters ~ 25 + 5n), so eps_t is a measured quantity rather than an assumption
checks.detail: refreshes 1..11; achieved eps_t = 9.943e-05 at the first and 9.995e-07 at the last

checks.name: WEAK DUALITY: the certified lower bound never exceeds a primal value, so the stopping certificate is on the safe side of the infimum
checks.detail: checked on 4 regions where a primal solve also succeeded; worst excess 5.40e-13

checks.name: and it is not merely safe but tight where both are available, so the certificate does not throw the stopping time away
the answer-selection set was recorded at every oracle refresh, so the selection rule can be audited rather than trusted
every stopped run stored the statistic that fired and the threshold it cleared, with a strictly positive margin -- so the stop can be rechecked from the artifact without rerunning anything
on a world whose correct answer is second in the tie-break, every stopped run still returns it -- so the rule is not merely reading off the tie-break
SELECTION RULE: a clearly suboptimal answer is dropped once the radius is small enough, so the rule can narrow the set at all
SELECTION RULE: the same inputs with a large radius keep both answers, so the rule is conservative rather than trigger-happy
SELECTION RULE: across a grid of brackets and radii the answer with the largest certified lower bracket is NEVER dropped -- the property the correctness proof needs
no escape hatch that would compromise the stopping guarantee fired, and every counter is written to the artifact whether it fired or not
